Sword: This Pokémon uses its psychic powers while it sleeps. The contents of Abra’s dreams affect the powers that the Pokémon wields.\n\nShield: Abra can teleport in its sleep. Apparently the more deeply Abra sleeps, the farther its teleportations go.

Sword: It has an incredibly high level of intelligence. Some say that Alakazam remembers everything that ever happens to it, from birth till death.\n\nShield: Alakazam wields potent psychic powers. It’s said that this Pokémon used these powers to create the spoons it holds.

Sword: At times, Magnemite runs out of electricity and ends up on the ground. If you give batteries to a grounded Magnemite, it’ll start moving again.\n\nShield: It subsists on electricity. As Magnemite flies, it emits electromagnetic waves from the units on each side of its body.

Sword: This Pokémon is three Magnemite that have linked together. Magneton sends out powerful radio waves to study its surroundings.\n\nShield: This Pokémon is constantly putting out a powerful magnetic force. Most computers go haywire when a Magneton approaches.

Sword: The stalk this Pokémon carries in its wings serves as a sword to cut down opponents. Sword: When Tauros begins whipping itself with its tails, it’s a warning that the Pokémon is about to charge with astounding speed.\n\nShield: The Tauros of the Galar region are volatile in nature, and they won’t allow people to ride on their backs.

column3: Sword: It has an extremely aggressive nature. The Hyper Beam it shoots from its mouth totally incinerates all targets.\n\nShield: Once it begins to rampage, a Gyarados will burn everything down, even in a harsh storm.

Sword: It has the ability to alter the composition of its body to suit its surrounding environment.\n\nShield: Thanks to its unstable genetic makeup, this special Pokémon conceals many different possible evolutions.

Sword: Once it has stored up enough heat, this Pokémon’s body temperature can reach up to 1,700 degrees Fahrenheit.\n\nShield: It stores some of the air it inhales in its internal flame pouch, which heats it to over 3,000 degrees Fahrenheit.

Sword: State-of-the-art technology was used to create Porygon. It was the first artificial Pokémon to be created via computer programming.\n\nShield: In recent years, this species has been very helpful in cyberspace. These Pokémon will go around checking to make sure no suspicious data exists.

Sword: Weighed down by a large and heavy shell, Omastar couldn’t move very fast. Some say it went extinct because it was unable to catch food.\n\nShield: Omastar’s sharp fangs could crush rock, but the Pokémon can attack only the prey that come within reach of its tentacles.

Sword: This species is almost entirely extinct. Kabuto molt every three days, making their shells harder and harder.\n\nShield: While some say this species has gone extinct, Kabuto sightings are apparently fairly common in some places.

Sword: Kabutops slices its prey apart and sucks out the fluids. The discarded body parts become food for other Pokémon.\n\nShield: The cause behind the extinction of this species is unknown. Kabutops were aggressive Pokémon that inhabited warm seas.

Sword: This is a ferocious Pokémon from ancient times. Apparently even modern technology is incapable of producing a perfectly restored specimen.\n\nShield: Aerodactyl’s sawlike fangs can shred skin to tatters—even the skin of Steel-type Pokémon.

Sword: It is not satisfied unless it eats over 880 pounds of food every day. When it is done eating, it goes promptly to sleep.\n\nShield: This Pokémon’s stomach is so strong, even eating moldy or rotten food will not affect it.

Sword: Although unattractive and unpopular, this Pokémon’s marvelous vitality has made it a subject of research.\n\nShield: It is a shabby and ugly Pokémon. However, it is very hardy and can survive on little water.

Sword: Because the magnetic powers of these Pokémon get stronger in freezing temperatures, Metagross living on snowy mountains are full of energy.\n\nShield: Metagross is the result of the fusion of two Metang. This Pokémon defeats its opponents through use of its supercomputer-level brain.

Sword: Every bit of Regirock’s body is made of stone. As parts of its body erode, this Pokémon sticks rocks to itself to repair what’s been lost.\n\nShield: Cutting-edge technology was used to study the internals of this Pokémon’s rock body, but nothing was found—not even a brain or a heart.

Sword: With cold air that can reach temperatures as low as −328 degrees Fahrenheit, Regice instantly freezes any creature that approaches it.\n\nShield: This Pokémon’s body is made of solid ice. It’s said that Regice was born beneath thick ice in the ice age.

Sword: Registeel’s body is made of a strange material that is flexible enough to stretch and shrink but also more durable than any metal.\n\nShield: It’s rumored that this Pokémon was born deep underground in the planet’s mantle and that it emerged onto the surface 10,000 years ago.

Sword: Once every 1,000 years, the singing of a pure voice will rouse this Pokémon from its near-perpetual slumber. It wakes for only seven days.\n\nShield: It’s believed that when this Pokémon wakes from its 1,000-year slumber, it will grant any wishes written on the notes attached to its head.

Sword: True to its honorable-warrior image, it uses the blades on its elbows only in defense of something or someone.\n\nShield: Sharply attuned to others’ wishes for help, this Pokémon seeks out those in need and aids them in battle.

Sword: By taking in a person’s scent, it can sniff out their mental and physical condition. It’s hoped that this skill will have many medical applications.\n\nShield: Slurpuff’s fur contains a lot of air, making it soft to the touch and lighter than it looks.

column2: Route 7, 9, Bridge Field, Hammerlocke Hills, Challenge Beach, Fields of Honor, Loop Lagoon, Training Lowlands
column3: Sword: It spins while making its luminescent spots flash. These spots allow it to communicate with others by using different patterns of light.\n\nShield: By exposing foes to the blinking of its luminescent spots, Inkay demoralizes them, and then it seizes the chance to flee.

Sword: Gazing at its luminescent spots will quickly induce a hypnotic state, putting the observer under Malamar’s control.\n\nShield: It’s said that Malamar’s hypnotic powers played a role in certain history-changing events.

column2: Bridge Field, Motostoke Riverbank, Galar Mine No. 2
column3: Sword: After two Binacle find a suitably sized rock, they adhere themselves to it and live together. They cooperate to gather food during high tide.\n\nShield: If the two don’t work well together, both their offense and defense fall apart. Without good teamwork, they won’t survive.

column2: Route 9, Dusty Bowl, Lake of Outrage
column3: Sword: Seven Binacle come together to form one Barbaracle. The Binacle that serves as the head gives orders to those serving as the limbs.\n\nShield: Having an eye on each palm allows it to keep watch in all directions. In a pinch, its limbs start to act on their own to ensure the enemy’s defeat.

Sword: It drifts in the ocean, blending in with floating seaweed. When other Pokémon come to feast on the seaweed, Skrelp feasts on them instead.\n\nShield: Skrelp looks like a piece of rotten seaweed, so it can blend in with seaweed drifting on the ocean and avoid being detected by enemies.

Sword: Dragalge uses a poisonous liquid capable of corroding metal to send tankers that enter its territory to the bottom of the sea.\n\nShield: Dragalge generates dragon energy by sticking the plume on its head out above the ocean’s surface and bathing it in sunlight.

column2: Honeycalm Island, Honeycalm Sea, Insular Sea, Stepping-Stone Sea, Workout Sea
column3: Sword: Clauncher’s claws can fall off during battle, but they’ll regenerate. The meat inside the claws is popular as a delicacy in Galar.\n\nShield: By detonating gas that accumulates in its right claw, this Pokémon launches water like a bullet. This is how Clauncher defeats its enemies.

column2: Honeycalm Island, Honeycalm Sea, Insular Sea, Stepping-Stone Sea, Workout Sea
column3: Sword: After using the feelers on its oversized claw to detect the location of prey, Clawitzer launches a cannonball of water at its target.\n\nShield: Clawitzer’s right arm is a cannon that launches projectiles made of seawater. Shots from a Clawitzer’s cannon arm can sink a tanker.

Sword: When spread, the frills on its head act like solar panels, generating the power behind this Pokémon’s electric moves.\n\nShield: The sun powers this Pokémon’s electricity generation. Interruption of that process stresses Helioptile to the point of weakness.

Sword: A now-vanished desert culture treasured these Pokémon. Appropriately, when Heliolisk came to the Galar region, treasure came with them.\n\nShield: One Heliolisk basking in the sun with its frill outspread is all it would take to produce enough electricity to power a city.

Sword: This is an ancient Pokémon, revived in modern times. It has a violent disposition, and it’ll tear apart anything it gets between its hefty jaws.\n\nShield: This Pokémon is selfish and likes to be pampered. It can also inflict grievous wounds on its Trainer just by playing around.

Sword: This Pokémon is from about 100,000,000 years ago. It has the presence of a king, vicious but magnificent.\n\nShield: A single bite of Tyrantrum’s massive jaws will demolish a car. This Pokémon was the king of the ancient world.

column2: Slippery Slope, Frostpoint Field, Snowslide Slope
column3: Sword: This Pokémon was successfully restored from a fossil. In the past, it lived with others of its kind in cold lands where there were fewer predators.\n\nShield: Amaura is an ancient Pokémon that has gone extinct. Specimens of this species can sometimes be found frozen in ice.

Sword: Aurorus was restored from a fossil. It’s said that when this Pokémon howls, auroras appear in the night sky.\n\nShield: When gripped by rage, Aurorus will emanate freezing air, covering everything around it in ice.

Sword: By releasing enmity-erasing waves from its ribbonlike feelers, Sylveon stops any conflict.\n\nShield: There’s a Galarian fairy tale that describes a beautiful Sylveon vanquishing a dreadful dragon Pokémon.

Sword: It drives its opponents to exhaustion with its agile maneuvers, then ends the fight with a flashy finishing move.\n\nShield: It always strikes a pose before going for its finishing move. Sometimes opponents take advantage of that time to counterattack.

Sword: A Dedenne’s whiskers pick up electrical waves other Dedenne send out. These Pokémon share locations of food or electricity with one another.\n\nShield: Since Dedenne can’t generate much electricity on its own, it steals electricity from outlets or other electric Pokémon.

column2: Tunnel to the Top, Roaring-Sea Caves, Lakeside Cave
column3: Sword: When beset by attackers, Carbink wipes them all out by firing high-energy beams from the gems embedded in its body.\n\nShield: It’s said that somewhere in the world, there’s a mineral vein housing a large pack of slumbering Carbink. It’s also said that this pack has a queen.

Sword: Because most of its body is water, it will dry up if the weather becomes too arid. It’s considered the weakest dragon Pokémon.\n\nShield: Their horns are powerful sensors. As soon as Goomy pick up any sign of enemies, they go into hiding. This is how they’ve survived.

Sword: Although this Pokémon isn’t very strong, its body is coated in a caustic slime that can melt through anything, so predators steer clear of it.\n\nShield: The lump on its back contains its tiny brain. It thinks only of food and escaping its enemies.

Sword: Sometimes it misunderstands instructions and appears dazed or bewildered. Many Trainers don’t mind, finding this behavior to be adorable.\n\nShield: Its form of offense is forcefully stretching out its horns. The strikes land 100 times harder than any blow from a heavyweight boxer.

Sword: This Pokémon is constantly collecting keys. Entrust a Klefki with important keys, and the Pokémon will protect them no matter what.\n\nShield: Klefki sucks in metal ions with the horn topping its head. It seems this Pokémon loves keys so much that its head needed to look like one, too.

column2: Glimwood Tangle, Slippery Slope, Old Cemetery, Snowslide Slope, Giant's Foot, Three-Point Pass
column3: Sword: After a lost child perished in the forest, their spirit possessed a tree stump, causing the spirit’s rebirth as this Pokémon.\n\nShield: With a voice like a human child’s, it cries out to lure adults deep into the forest, getting them lost among the trees.

Sword: People fear it due to a belief that it devours any who try to cut down trees in its forest, but to the Pokémon it shares its woods with, it’s kind.\n\nShield: Small roots that extend from the tips of this Pokémon’s feet can tie into the trees of the forest and give Trevenant control over them.

column2: Route 9, Lake of Outrage, Frigid Sea, Three-Point Pass
column3: Sword: They chill the air around them to −150 degrees Fahrenheit, freezing the water in the air into ice that they use as armor.\n\nShield: This Pokémon lives in areas of frigid cold. It secures itself to the back of an Avalugg by freezing its feet in place.

Sword: At high latitudes, this Pokémon can be found with clusters of Bergmite on its back as it swims among the icebergs.\n\nShield: As Avalugg moves about during the day, the cracks in its body deepen. The Pokémon’s body returns to a pristine state overnight.

column2: Bridge Field, Watchtower Ruins, Galar Mine No. 2
column3: Sword: After nightfall, they emerge from the caves they nest in during the day. Using their ultrasonic waves, they go on the hunt for ripened fruit.\n\nShield: No wavelength of sound is beyond Noibat’s ability to produce. The ultrasonic waves it generates can overcome much larger Pokémon.

column2: Lake of Outrage, Ballimere Lake, Lakeside Cave
column3: Sword: Aggressive and cruel, this Pokémon will ruthlessly torment enemies that are helpless in the dark.\n\nShield: Flying through the darkness, it weakens enemies with ultrasonic waves that could crush stone. Its fangs finish the fight.

Sword: At a distance, it launches its sharp feathers while flying about. If the enemy gets too close, Rowlet switches tactics and delivers vicious kicks.\n\nShield: During the day, it builds up energy via photosynthesis. At night, it flies silently through the sky, on the prowl for prey.

Sword: It throws one knifelike feather after another at its enemies, and each one precisely strikes a weak point. These feathers are known as blade quills.\n\nShield: It never slacks when it comes to the task of cleaning its feathers. Thorough preening keeps it looking spiffy and its blade quills nice and sharp.

Sword: As if wielding a bow, it launches the arrow quills hidden among the feathers of its wings. Decidueye’s shots never miss.\n\nShield: In a tenth of a second, it can nock and fire an arrow quill, piercing an opponent’s weak point before they notice what’s happening.

Sword: It spends even the smallest amount of downtime grooming its fur with its tongue. Loose fur gathers in its stomach and serves as fuel for fiery moves.\n\nShield: Trying to pet Litten before it trusts you will result in a nasty scratch from its sharp claws. Be careful.

Sword: In the midst of battle, the fire pouch on Torracat’s neck rings like a bell and produces stronger flames than usual.\n\nShield: When facing a powerful enemy, Torracat’s fighting spirit gets pumped up, and its fire bell blazes hotter.

Sword: It excels at violent, no-holds-barred battles. The temperature of the flames that issue from its navel exceeds 3,600 degrees Fahrenheit.\n\nShield: Incineroar’s rough and aggressive behavior is its most notable trait, but the way it helps out small Pokémon shows that it has a kind side as well.

Sword: It creates special bouncy balloons to send at its opponents. When the balloons pop, the sheer force of their bursting is what deals damage.\n\nShield: If Popplio want to create big, powerful balloons, they must be persistent. It takes daily practice for these Pokémon to develop their skills.

Sword: As if dancing, it artfully dodges the attacks of its enemies. All the while, it’s busy forming a bunch of balloons to overwhelm its foes.\n\nShield: On nights when the sea is calm, Brionne dance with one another to the singing of the Primarina that’s leading them.

Sword: With its mouth, it makes sonic waves that sound like beautiful singing. It uses the sonic waves to control its water balloons.\n\nShield: For Primarina, every battle’s a stage. Its singing and the dancing of its balloons will mesmerize the audience.

column2: Route 1, East Lake Axewell, Slumbering Weald, Dappled Grove, North Lake Miloch, Watchtower Ruins
column3: Sword: Its natural enemies, like Rookidee, may flee rather than risk getting caught in its large mandibles that can snap thick tree branches.\n\nShield: It uses its big jaws to dig nests into the forest floor, and it loves to feed on sweet tree sap.

column2: Axew's Eye, Dusty Bowl, Hammerlocke Hills
column3: Sword: While its durable shell protects it from attacks, Charjabug strikes at enemies with jolts of electricity discharged from the tips of its jaws.\n\nShield: Its digestive processes convert the leaves it eats into electricity. An electric sac in its belly stores the electricity for later use.

Sword: It builds up electricity in its abdomen, focuses it through its jaws, and then fires the electricity off in concentrated beams.\n\nShield: If it carries a Charjabug to use as a spare battery, a flying Vikavolt can rapidly fire high-powered beams of electricity.

column2: Route 4, Bridge Field, Giant's Mirror, Motostoke Riverbank
column3: Sword: Nectar and pollen are its favorite fare. You can find Cutiefly hovering around Gossifleur, trying to get some of Gossifleur’s pollen.\n\nShield: An opponent’s aura can tell Cutiefly what that opponent’s next move will be. Then Cutiefly can glide around the attack and strike back.

Sword: It makes pollen puffs from pollen and nectar. The puffs’ effects depend on the type of ingredients and how much of each one is used.\n\nShield: Ribombee absolutely hate getting wet or rained on. In the cloudy Galar region, they are very seldom seen.

Sword: This Pokémon can bond very strongly with its Trainer, but it also has a habit of biting. Raising a Rockruff for a long time can be challenging.\n\nShield: This Pokémon intimidates opponents by striking the ground with the rocks on its neck. The moment an opponent flinches, Rockruff attacks.

Sword: This Lycanroc is calm and cautious. The rocks jutting from its mane are razor sharp.\n\nShield: With swift movements, this Pokémon gradually backs its prey into a corner. Lycanroc’s fangs are always aimed toward opponents’ weak spots.

column2: Route 9, East Lake Axewell, Axew's Eye, West Lake Axewell, Hulbury, Challenge Beach, Honeycalm Island, Honeycalm Sea, Insular Sea, Stepping-Stone Sea
column3: Sword: Individually, they’re incredibly weak. It’s by gathering up into schools that they’re able to confront opponents.\n\nShield: When it senses danger, its eyes tear up. The sparkle of its tears signals other Wishiwashi to gather.

column2: Route 9, Giant's Mirror, Motostoke Riverbank, Loop Lagoon
column3: Sword: The first symptom of its sting is numbness. The next is an itching sensation so intense that it’s impossible to resist the urge to claw at your skin.\n\nShield: Unlike their Alolan counterparts, the Mareanie of the Galar region have not yet figured out that the branches of Corsola are delicious.

Sword: To survive in the cold waters of Galar, this Pokémon forms a dome with its legs, enclosing its body so it can capture its own body heat.\n\nShield: Within the poison sac in its body is a poison so toxic that Pokémon as large as Wailord will still be suffering three days after it first takes effect.

column2: Route 3, Rolling Fields, South Lake Miloch, East Lake Axewell, Dappled Grove, West Lake Axewell, Giant's Cap, Giant's Seat, North Lake Miloch
column3: Sword: Loads weighing up to 50 times as much as its own body weight pose no issue for this Pokémon. It’s skilled at making use of mud.\n\nShield: It eats dirt to create mud and smears this mud all over its feet, giving them the grip needed to walk on rough terrain without slipping.

column2: Axew's Eye, Dusty Bowl, Giant's Seat
column3: Sword: Mud that hardens around a Mudsdale’s legs sets harder than stone. It’s so hard that it allows this Pokémon to scrap a truck with a single kick.\n\nShield: Mudsdale has so much stamina that it could carry over 10 tons across the Galar region without rest or sleep.

column2: Route 5, Motostoke Riverbank, Stony Wilderness, Giant's Bed, Old Cemetery, Giant's Foot, Frigid Sea, Three-Point Pass, Ballimere Lake
column3: Sword: It forms a water bubble at the rear of its body and then covers its head with it. Meeting another Dewpider means comparing water-bubble sizes.\n\nShield: Dewpider normally lives underwater. When it comes onto land in search of food, it takes water with it in the form of a bubble on its head.

column2: Lake of Outrage, Giant's Bed, Old Cemetery, Giant's Foot, Frigid Sea, Three-Point Pass, Ballimere Lake
column3: Sword: It launches water bubbles with its legs, drowning prey within the bubbles. This Pokémon can then take its time to savor its meal.\n\nShield: It acts as a caretaker for Dewpider, putting them inside its bubble and letting them eat any leftover food.

column2: Challenge Beach, Fields of Honor, Forest of Focus, Soothing Wetlands, Training Lowlands
column3: Sword: When bathed in sunlight, this Pokémon emits a pleasantly sweet scent, which causes bug Pokémon to gather around it.\n\nShield: During the day, Fomantis basks in sunlight and sleeps peacefully. It wakes and moves around at night.

Sword: This Pokémon resembles a beautiful flower. A properly raised Lurantis will have gorgeous, brilliant colors.\n\nShield: The petals on this Pokémon’s arms are thin and super sharp, and they can fire laser beams if Lurantis gathers light first.

Sword: Pokémon living in the forest eat the delicious caps on Morelull’s head. The caps regrow overnight.\n\nShield: Morelull live in forests that stay dark even during the day. They scatter flickering spores that put enemies to sleep.

Sword: Its flickering spores lure in prey and put them to sleep. Once this Pokémon has its prey snoozing, it drains their vitality with its fingertips.\n\nShield: If you see a light deep in a forest at night, don’t go near. Shiinotic will make you fall fast asleep.

Sword: Its venom sacs produce a fluid that this Pokémon then heats up with the flame in its tail. This process creates Salandit’s poisonous gas.\n\nShield: This sneaky Pokémon will slink behind its prey and immobilize it with poisonous gas before the prey even realizes Salandit is there.

Sword: Only female Salazzle exist. They emit a gas laden with pheromones to captivate male Salandit.\n\nShield: The winner of competitions between Salazzle is decided by which one has the most male Salandit with it.

column2: Route 5, East Lake Axewell, Bridge Field, Dappled Grove, Giant's Seat, Hammerlocke Hills, North Lake Miloch
column3: Sword: Its fluffy fur is a delight to pet, but carelessly reaching out to touch this Pokémon could result in painful retaliation.\n\nShield: The way it protects itself by flailing its arms may be an adorable sight, but stay well away. This is flailing that can snap thick tree trunks.

column2: Axew's Eye, Giant's Seat, Lake of Outrage
column3: Sword: Once it accepts you as a friend, it tries to show its affection with a hug. Letting it do that is dangerous—it could easily shatter your bones.\n\nShield: The moves it uses to take down its prey would make a martial artist jealous. It tucks subdued prey under its arms to carry them to its nest.

column2: Rolling Fields, East Lake Axewell, Dappled Grove, West Lake Axewell, Stony Wilderness, Watchtower Ruins
column3: Sword: Its body gives off a sweet, fruity scent that is extremely appetizing to bird Pokémon.\n\nShield: When under attack, it secretes a sweet and delicious sweat. The scent only calls more enemies to it.

Sword: As it twirls like a dancer, a sweet smell spreads out around it. Anyone who inhales the scent will feel a surge of happiness.\n\nShield: Any Corvisquire that pecks at this Pokémon will be greeted with a smack from its sepals followed by a sharp kick.

Sword: This feared Pokémon has long, slender legs and a cruel heart. It shows no mercy as it stomps on its opponents.\n\nShield: A kick from the hardened tips of this Pokémon’s legs leaves a wound in the opponent’s body and soul that will never heal.

Sword: Comfey picks flowers with its vine and decorates itself with them. For some reason, flowers won’t wither once they’re attached to a Comfey.\n\nShield: These Pokémon smell very nice. All Comfey wear different flowers, so each of these Pokémon has its own individual scent.

Sword: With waves of its fan—made from leaves and its own fur—Oranguru skillfully gives instructions to other Pokémon.\n\nShield: It knows the forest inside and out. If it comes across a wounded Pokémon, Oranguru will gather medicinal herbs to treat it.

Sword: Displaying amazing teamwork, they follow the orders of their boss as they all help out in the search for their favorite berries.\n\nShield: Passimian live in groups of about 20, with each member performing an assigned role. Through cooperation, the group survives.

column2: Bridge Field, Giant's Mirror, Hammerlocke Hills, Motostoke Riverbank, Galar Mine No. 2, Courageous Cavern
column3: Sword: It’s nature’s cleaner—it eats anything and everything, including garbage and rotten things. The ground near its nest is always clean.\n\nShield: Wimpod gather in swarms, constantly on the lookout for danger. They scatter the moment they detect an enemy’s presence.

Sword: It will do anything to win, taking advantage of every opening and finishing opponents off with the small claws on its front legs.\n\nShield: They live in sunken ships or in holes in the seabed. When Golisopod and Grapploct battle, the loser becomes the winner’s meal.

Sword: Grudges of the dead have possessed a mound of sand and become a Pokémon. Sandygast is fond of the shovel on its head.\n\nShield: Sandygast mainly inhabits beaches. It takes control of anyone who puts their hand into its mouth, forcing them to make its body bigger.

Sword: Palossand is known as the Beach Nightmare. It pulls its prey down into the sand by controlling the sand itself, and then it sucks out their souls.\n\nShield: This Pokémon lives on beaches, but it hates water. Palossand can’t maintain its castle-like shape if it gets drenched by a heavy rain.

column2: Route 9, South Lake Miloch, Giant's Seat
column3: Sword: It lives in warm, shallow waters. If it encounters a foe, it will spit out its internal organs as a means to punch them.\n\nShield: It’s covered in a slime that keeps its skin moist, allowing it to stay on land for days without drying up.

Sword: Rumor has it that the theft of top-secret research notes led to a new instance of this Pokémon being created in the Galar region.\n\nShield: It was modeled after a mighty Pokémon of myth. The mask placed upon it limits its power in order to keep it under control.

Sword: A solid bond of trust between this Pokémon and its Trainer awakened the strength hidden within Silvally. It can change its type at will.\n\nShield: The final factor needed to release this Pokémon’s true power was a strong bond with a Trainer it trusts.

Sword: Explosive substances coat the shell on its back. Enemies that dare attack it will be blown away by an immense detonation.\n\nShield: Eating sulfur in its volcanic habitat is what causes explosive compounds to develop in its shell. Its droppings are also dangerously explosive.

Sword: With the long hairs on its back, this Pokémon takes in electricity from other electric Pokémon. It stores what it absorbs in an electric sac.\n\nShield: When it’s in trouble, it curls up into a ball, makes its fur spikes stand on end, and then discharges electricity indiscriminately.

column2: Giant's Mirror, Slippery Slope, Frostpoint Field, Giant's Bed, Old Cemetery, Snowslide Slope, Giant's Foot, Frigid Sea, Three-Point Pass, Ballimere Lake
column3: Sword: There will be no forgiveness for any who reveal that it was pretending to be Pikachu. It will bring the culprit down, even at the cost of its own life.\n\nShield: Its disguise made from an old rag allowed it to avoid an attack, but the impact broke the neck of the disguise. Now everyone knows it’s a Mimikyu.

Sword: The mountains it calls home are nearly two miles in height. On rare occasions, it descends to play with the children living in the towns below.\n\nShield: Drampa is a kind and friendly Pokémon—up until it’s angered. When that happens, it stirs up a gale and flattens everything around.

Sword: After a piece of seaweed merged with debris from a sunken ship, it was reborn as this ghost Pokémon.\n\nShield: After lowering its anchor, it waits for its prey. It catches large Wailord and drains their life-force.

column2: Lake of Outrage, Challenge Road, Potbottom Desert
column3: Sword: They learn to fight by smashing their head scales together. The dueling strengthens both their skills and their spirits.\n\nShield: Jangmo-o strikes its scales to communicate with others of its kind. Its scales are actually fur that’s become as hard as metal.

Sword: The scaleless, scarred parts of its body are signs of its strength. It shows them off to defeated opponents.\n\nShield: Before attacking its enemies, it clashes its scales together and roars. Its sharp claws shred the opposition.

Sword: It clatters its tail scales to unnerve opponents. This Pokémon will battle only those who stand steadfast in the face of this display.\n\nShield: Certain ruins have paintings of ancient warriors wearing armor made of Kommo-o scales.

Sword: This Pokémon came from another universe. Its gaseous body is so light that even a gentle breeze can blow it away.\n\nShield: Cosmog is very curious but not very cautious, often placing itself in danger. If things start to look dicey, it teleports away.

Sword: The absorption of starlight fuels this Pokémon’s growth. The shell that encases it is harder than any known material.\n\nShield: It sucks in dust from the air at an astounding rate, frantically building up energy within its core as preparation for evolution.

Sword: When light radiates from its body, this Pokémon could almost appear to be the sun. It will dispel any darkness and light up the world.\n\nShield: Solgaleo was once known as the Beast That Devours the Sun. Energy in the form of light radiates boundlessly from it.

Sword: Known as the Beast That Calls the Moon, this Pokémon lives by taking in any and all light and converting it into its own energy.\n\nShield: It steals the light from its surroundings and then becomes the full moon, showering its own light across the night sky.

Sword: It survives by absorbing light. After a long time spent slumbering underground, impurities accumulated within it, causing its body to darken.\n\nShield: It needs light to survive, and it goes on a rampage seeking it out. Its laser beams will cut anything to pieces.

Sword: By slipping into the shadow of a martial arts master and copying their movements, this Pokémon learned the ultimate techniques.\n\nShield: This Pokémon can conceal itself in any shadow, so it went undiscovered for a long time.

Sword: It runs as fast as lightning strikes, shredding its opponents with its high-voltage claws.\n\nShield: Electricity sparks from the pads on its limbs. Wherever Zeraora runs, lightning flashes and thunder echoes.

Sword: It dissolves and eats metal. Circulating liquid metal within its body is how it generates energy.\n\nShield: They live as a group, but when the time comes, one strong Meltan will absorb all the others and evolve.

Sword: At the end of its life-span, Melmetal will rust and fall apart. The small shards left behind will eventually be reborn as Meltan.\n\nShield: Centrifugal force is behind the punches of Melmetal’s heavy hex-nut arms. Melmetal is said to deliver the strongest punches of all Pokémon.

Sword: When it uses its special stick to strike up a beat, the sound waves produced carry revitalizing energy to the plants and flowers in the area.\n\nShield: It attacks with rapid beats of its stick. As it strikes with amazing speed, it gets more and more pumped.

Sword: The faster a Thwackey can beat out a rhythm with its two sticks, the more respect it wins from its peers.\n\nShield: When it’s drumming out rapid beats in battle, it gets so caught up in the rhythm that it won’t even notice that it’s already knocked out its opponent.

Sword: By drumming, it taps into the power of its special tree stump. The roots of the stump follow its direction in battle.\n\nShield: The one with the best drumming techniques becomes the boss of the troop. It has a gentle disposition and values harmony among its group.

Sword: A warm-up of running around gets fire energy coursing through this Pokémon’s body. Once that happens, it’s ready to fight at full power.\n\nShield: It has special pads on the backs of its feet, and one on its nose. Once it’s raring to fight, these pads radiate tremendous heat.

Sword: Its thick and fluffy fur protects it from the cold and enables it to use hotter fire moves.\n\nShield: It kicks berries right off the branches of trees and then juggles them with its feet, practicing its footwork.

Sword: It juggles a pebble with its feet, turning it into a burning soccer ball. Its shots strike opponents hard and leave them scorched.\n\nShield: It’s skilled at both offense and defense, and it gets pumped up when cheered on. But if it starts showboating, it could put itself in a tough spot.

Sword: When scared, this Pokémon cries. Its tears pack the chemical punch of 100 onions, and attackers won’t be able to resist weeping.\n\nShield: When it gets wet, its skin changes color, and this Pokémon becomes invisible as if it were camouflaged.

Sword: A clever combatant, this Pokémon battles using water balloons created with moisture secreted from its palms.\n\nShield: Highly intelligent but also very lazy, it keeps enemies out of its territory by laying traps everywhere.

Sword: It has many hidden capabilities, such as fingertips that can shoot water and a membrane on its back that it can use to glide through the air.\n\nShield: Its nictitating membranes let it pick out foes’ weak points so it can precisely blast them with water that shoots from its fingertips at Mach 3.

column2: Route 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, Rolling Fields, Slumbering Weald, Dappled Grove, Motostoke Riverbank, North Lake Miloch, Watchtower Ruins, Challenge Beach, Fields of Honor, Forest of Focus, Insular Sea, Loop Lagoon, Soothing Wetlands, Stepping-Stone Sea, Training Lowlands, Workout Sea, Slippery Slope, Frostpoint Field, Giant's Bed, Giant's Foot, Ballimere Lake
column3: Sword: Found throughout the Galar region, this Pokémon becomes uneasy if its cheeks are ever completely empty of berries.\n\nShield: It eats berries nonstop—a habit that has made it more resilient than it looks. It’ll show up on farms, searching for yet more berries.

column2: Route 6, 7, 9, Axew's Eye, Bridge Field, Giant's Cap, Giant's Mirror, Giant's Seat, Hammerlocke Hills, Lake of Outrage, Motostoke Riverbank, Slippery Slope, Frostpoint Field, Giant's Bed, Giant's Foot, Ballimere Lake
column3: Sword: It stashes berries in its tail—so many berries that they fall out constantly. But this Pokémon is a bit slow-witted, so it doesn’t notice the loss.\n\nShield: Common throughout the Galar region, this Pokémon has strong teeth and can chew through the toughest of berry shells.

Sword: It will bravely challenge any opponent, no matter how powerful. This Pokémon benefits from every battle—even a defeat increases its strength a bit.\n\nShield: Jumping nimbly about, this small-bodied Pokémon takes advantage of even the slightest opportunity to disorient larger opponents.

column2: Giant's Mirror, Hammerlocke Hills, Motostoke Riverbank, Ballimere Lake
column3: Sword: Smart enough to use tools in battle, these Pokémon have been seen picking up rocks and flinging them or using ropes to wrap up enemies.\n\nShield: The lessons of many harsh battles have taught it how to accurately judge an opponent’s strength.

column2: Route 7, Slumbering Weald, Dusty Bowl, Lake of Outrage
column3: Sword: This Pokémon reigns supreme in the skies of the Galar region. The black luster of its steel body could drive terror into the heart of any foe.\n\nShield: With their great intellect and flying skills, these Pokémon very successfully act as the Galar region’s airborne taxi service.

column2: Route 1, 2, Slumbering Weald, Giant's Cap, Challenge Beach, Challenge Road, Fields of Honor, Honeycalm Island, Insular Sea, Loop Lagoon, Stepping-Stone Sea, Training Lowlands, Workout Sea
column3: Sword: A constant collector of information, this Pokémon is very smart. Very strong is what it isn’t.\n\nShield: Often found in gardens, this Pokémon has hairs on its body that it uses to assess its surroundings.

column2: Route 5, Giant's Cap, Giant's Mirror, Stony Wilderness
column3: Sword: It barely moves, but it’s still alive. Hiding in its shell without food or water seems to have awakened its psychic powers.\n\nShield: As it grows inside its shell, it uses its psychic abilities to monitor the outside world and prepare for evolution.

Sword: It’s famous for its high level of intelligence, and the large size of its brain is proof that it also possesses immense psychic power.\n\nShield: It emits psychic energy to observe and study what’s around it—and what’s around it can include things over six miles away.

column2: Route 1, 2, Dusty Bowl, Giant's Mirror, Stony Wilderness
column3: Sword: Aided by the soft pads on its feet, it silently raids the food stores of other Pokémon. It survives off its ill-gotten gains.\n\nShield: Cunning and cautious, this Pokémon survives by stealing food from others. It erases its tracks with swipes of its tail as it makes off with its plunder.

column2: Route 7, 9, Bridge Field, Hammerlocke Hills, Stony Wilderness
column3: Sword: It secretly marks potential targets with a scent. By following the scent, it stalks its targets and steals from them when they least expect it.\n\nShield: With a lithe body and sharp claws, it goes around stealing food and eggs. Boltund is its natural enemy.

Sword: It anchors itself in the ground with its single leg, then basks in the sun. After absorbing enough sunlight, its petals spread as it blooms brilliantly.\n\nShield: It whirls around in the wind while singing a joyous song. This delightful display has charmed many into raising this Pokémon.

column2: Dusty Bowl, Giant's Cap, Motostoke Riverbank, Stony Wilderness
column3: Sword: The seeds attached to its cotton fluff are full of nutrients. It spreads them on the wind so that plants and other Pokémon can benefit from them.\n\nShield: The cotton on the head of this Pokémon can be spun into a glossy, gorgeous yarn—a Galar regional specialty.

column2: Route 1, 4, Motostoke Riverbank, Slippery Slope, Frostpoint Field, Giant's Bed, Snowslide Slope, Three-Point Pass
column3: Sword: Its curly fleece is such an effective cushion that this Pokémon could fall off a cliff and stand right back up at the bottom, unharmed.\n\nShield: If its fleece grows too long, Wooloo won’t be able to move. Cloth made with the wool of this Pokémon is surprisingly strong.

column2: Dusty Bowl, Hammerlocke Hills, Motostoke Riverbank, Slippery Slope, Frostpoint Field, Giant's Bed, Snowslide Slope, Three-Point Pass
column3: Sword: Weave a carpet from its springy wool, and you end up with something closer to a trampoline. You’ll start to bounce the moment you set foot on it.\n\nShield: Its majestic horns are meant only to impress the opposite gender. They never see use in battle.

column2: Route 2, 4, 5, Motostoke, Giant's Cap, Giant's Mirror, Motostoke Outskirts, Motostoke Riverbank, Hulbury, Galar Mine No. 2, Courageous Cavern, Soothing Wetlands
column3: Sword: Apparently the itch of its teething impels it to snap its jaws at anything in front of it.\n\nShield: It starts off battles by attacking with its rock-hard horn, but as soon as the opponent flinches, this Pokémon bites down and never lets go.

column2: Route 6, Bridge Field, Dusty Bowl, Giant's Cap, Giant's Mirror, Lake of Outrage
column3: Sword: With jaws that can shear through steel rods, this highly aggressive Pokémon chomps down on its unfortunate prey.\n\nShield: This Pokémon rapidly extends its retractable neck to sink its sharp fangs into distant enemies and take them down.

column2: Route 2, 4, Giant's Mirror, Motostoke Riverbank, Stony Wilderness, Ballimere Lake
column3: Sword: This Pokémon is very popular as a herding dog in the Galar region. As it runs, it generates electricity from the base of its tail.\n\nShield: This gluttonous Pokémon only assists people with their work because it wants treats. As it runs, it crackles with electricity.

column2: Dusty Bowl, Lake of Outrage, Motostoke Riverbank, Ballimere Lake
column3: Sword: This Pokémon generates electricity and channels it into its legs to keep them going strong. Boltund can run nonstop for three full days.\n\nShield: It sends electricity through its legs to boost their strength. Running at top speed, it easily breaks 50 mph.

column2: Route 3, Galar Mine, Giant's Cap, Motostoke Riverbank
column3: Sword: Most of its body has the same composition as coal. Fittingly, this Pokémon was first discovered in coal mines about 400 years ago.\n\nShield: It can race around like a unicycle, even on rough, rocky terrain. Burning coal sustains it.

column2: Bridge Field, Giant's Cap, Stony Wilderness, Ballimere Lake, Lakeside Cave
column3: Sword: It forms coal inside its body. Coal dropped by this Pokémon once helped fuel the lives of people in the Galar region.\n\nShield: By rapidly rolling its legs, it can travel at over 18 mph. The temperature of the flames it breathes exceeds 1,800 degrees Fahrenheit.

Sword: It’s usually peaceful, but the vandalism of mines enrages it. Offenders will be incinerated with flames that reach 2,700 degrees Fahrenheit.\n\nShield: While it’s engaged in battle, its mountain of coal will burn bright red, sending off sparks that scorch the surrounding area.

column2: Route 5, Dusty Bowl, Giant's Mirror, Stony Wilderness, Challenge Beach, Fields of Honor, Forest of Focus, Insular Sea, Loop Lagoon, Soothing Wetlands, Stepping-Stone Sea, Training Lowlands, Workout Sea
column3: Sword: It spends its entire life inside an apple. It hides from its natural enemies, bird Pokémon, by pretending it’s just an apple and nothing more.\n\nShield: As soon as it’s born, it burrows into an apple. Not only does the apple serve as its food source, but the flavor of the fruit determines its evolution.

Sword: It ate a sour apple, and that induced its evolution. In its cheeks, it stores an acid capable of causing chemical burns.\n\nShield: It flies on wings of apple skin and spits a powerful acid. It can also change its shape into that of an apple.

Sword: Eating a sweet apple caused its evolution. A nectarous scent wafts from its body, luring in the bug Pokémon it preys on.\n\nShield: Its body is covered in sweet nectar, and the skin on its back is especially yummy. Children used to have it as a snack.

column2: Route 6, Challenge Road, Forest of Focus, Potbottom Desert, Training Lowlands
column3: Sword: As it digs, it swallows sand and stores it in its neck pouch. The pouch can hold more than 17 pounds of sand.\n\nShield: It spews sand from its nostrils. While the enemy is blinded, it burrows into the ground to hide.

Sword: When it contracts its body, over 220 pounds of sand sprays from its nose. If it ever runs out of sand, it becomes disheartened.\n\nShield: Its unique style of coiling allows it to blast sand out of its sand sac more efficiently.

column2: Route 9, Bridge Field, Lake of Outrage, Stony Wilderness, Challenge Beach, Forest of Focus, Training Lowlands
column3: Sword: It’s so strong that it can knock out some opponents in a single hit, but it also may forget what it’s battling midfight.\n\nShield: This hungry Pokémon swallows Arrokuda whole. Occasionally, it makes a mistake and tries to swallow a Pokémon other than its preferred prey.

column2: Route 2, Motostoke Riverbank, Hulbury, Challenge Beach, Forest of Focus, Training Lowlands
column3: Sword: If it sees any movement around it, this Pokémon charges for it straightaway, leading with its sharply pointed jaw. It’s very proud of that jaw.\n\nShield: After it’s eaten its fill, its movements become extremely sluggish. That’s when Cramorant swallows it up.

column2: Route 2, Dusty Bowl, Lake of Outrage, Motostoke Riverbank
column3: Sword: This Pokémon has a jaw that’s as sharp as a spear and as strong as steel. Apparently Barraskewda’s flesh is surprisingly tasty, too.\n\nShield: It spins its tail fins to propel itself, surging forward at speeds of over 100 knots before ramming prey and spearing into them.

column2: Route 7, Bridge Field, Giant's Cap, Hammerlocke Hills, Motostoke Riverbank, Stony Wilderness
column3: Sword: It stores poison in an internal poison sac and secretes that poison through its skin. If you touch this Pokémon, a tingling sensation follows.\n\nShield: It manipulates the chemical makeup of its poison to produce electricity. The voltage is weak, but it can cause a tingling paralysis.

Sword: When this Pokémon sounds as if it’s strumming a guitar, it’s actually clawing at the protrusions on its chest to generate electricity.\n\nShield: This short-tempered and aggressive Pokémon chugs stagnant water to absorb any toxins it might contain.

Sword: It stores flammable gas in its body and uses it to generate heat. The yellow sections on its belly get particularly hot.\n\nShield: It wraps prey up with its heated body, cooking them in its coils. Once they’re well-done, it will voraciously nibble them down to the last morsel.

Sword: When it heats up, its body temperature reaches about 1,500 degrees Fahrenheit. It lashes its body like a whip and launches itself at enemies.\n\nShield: While its burning body is already dangerous on its own, this excessively hostile Pokémon also has large and very sharp fangs.

Sword: It’s very curious, but its means of investigating things is to try to punch them with its tentacles. The search for food is what brings it onto land.\n\nShield: Its tentacles tear off easily, but it isn’t alarmed when that happens—it knows they’ll grow back. It’s about as smart as a three-year-old.

Sword: A body made up of nothing but muscle makes the grappling moves this Pokémon performs with its tentacles tremendously powerful.\n\nShield: Searching for an opponent to test its skills against, it emerges onto land. Once the battle is over, it returns to the sea.

Sword: The swirl pattern in this Pokémon’s body is its weakness. If it gets stirred, the swirl loses its shape, and Sinistea gets dizzy.\n\nShield: It absorbs the life-force of those who drink it. It waits patiently, but opportunities are fleeting— it tastes so bad that it gets spat out immediately.

Sword: Trainers Polteageist trusts will be allowed to experience its distinctive flavor and aroma firsthand by sampling just a tiny bit of its tea.\n\nShield: When angered, it launches tea from its body at the offender’s mouth. The tea causes strong chills if swallowed.

column2: Hammerlocke Hills, Motostoke Outskirts, Stony Wilderness, Slippery Slope, Frostpoint Field, Giant's Bed, Old Cemetery, Giant's Foot, Frigid Sea, Three-Point Pass, Ballimere Lake
column3: Sword: Via the protrusion on its head, it senses other creatures’ emotions. If you don’t have a calm disposition, it will never warm up to you.\n\nShield: If this Pokémon senses a strong emotion, it will run away as fast as it can. It prefers areas without people.

column2: Glimwood Tangle, Dusty Bowl, Frostpoint Field, Giant's Bed, Old Cemetery, Giant's Foot, Frigid Sea, Three-Point Pass, Ballimere Lake
column3: Sword: No matter who you are, if you bring strong emotions near this Pokémon, it will silence you violently.\n\nShield: Using the braids on its head, it pummels foes to get them to quiet down. One blow from those braids would knock out a professional boxer.

Sword: It emits psychic power strong enough to cause headaches as a deterrent to the approach of others.\n\nShield: If you’re too loud around it, you risk being torn apart by the claws on its tentacle. This Pokémon is also known as the Forest Witch.

column2: Giant's Mirror, Hammerlocke Hills, Motostoke Outskirts, Stony Wilderness, Slippery Slope
column3: Sword: Through its nose, it sucks in the emanations produced by people and Pokémon when they feel annoyed. It thrives off this negative energy.\n\nShield: It sneaks into people’s homes, stealing things and feasting on the negative energy of the frustrated occupants.

column2: Glimwood Tangle, Giant's Bed, Snowslide Slope, Giant's Foot
column3: Sword: When it gets down on all fours as if to beg for forgiveness, it’s trying to lure opponents in so that it can stab them with its spear-like hair.\n\nShield: With sly cunning, it tries to lure people into the woods. Some believe it to have the power to make crops grow.

Sword: With the hair wrapped around its body helping to enhance its muscles, this Pokémon can overwhelm even Machamp.\n\nShield: Its hairs work like muscle fibers. When its hairs unfurl, they latch on to opponents, ensnaring them as tentacles would.

Sword: Its voice is staggering in volume. Obstagoon has a tendency to take on a threatening posture and shout—this move is known as Obstruct.\n\nShield: It evolved after experiencing numerous fights. While crossing its arms, it lets out a shout that would make any opponent flinch.

Sword: What appears to be an iron helmet is actually hardened hair. This Pokémon lives for the thrill of battle.\n\nShield: After many battles, it evolved dangerous claws that come together to form daggers when extended.

Sword: Its shell is overflowing with its heightened otherworldly energy. The ectoplasm serves as protection for this Pokémon’s core spirit.\n\nShield: Be cautious of the ectoplasmic body surrounding its soul. You’ll become stiff as stone if you touch it.

Sword: Only Farfetch’d that have survived many battles can attain this evolution. When this Pokémon’s leek withers, it will retire from combat.\n\nShield: After deflecting attacks with its hard leaf shield, it strikes back with its sharp leek stalk. The leek stalk is both weapon and food.

Sword: It’s highly skilled at tap-dancing. It waves its cane of ice in time with its graceful movements.\n\nShield: Its amusing movements make it very popular. It releases its psychic power from the pattern on its belly.

Sword: A powerful curse was woven into an ancient painting. After absorbing the spirit of a Yamask, the painting began to move.\n\nShield: Never touch its shadowlike body, or you’ll be shown the horrific memories behind the picture carved into it.
Sword: This Pokémon was born from sweet-smelling particles in the air. Its body is made of cream.\n\nShield: They say that any patisserie visited by Milcery is guaranteed success and good fortune.

Sword: The moment it evolved, it took on a bitter flavor. This is because of the way its cells spontaneously shifted during evolution.\n\nShield: The cells that compose its cream fluctuated suddenly during evolution, giving the cream a bitter flavor.

Sword: Five of them are troopers, and one is the brass. The brass’s orders are absolute.\n\nShield: The six of them work together as one Pokémon. Teamwork is also their battle strategy, and they constantly change their formation as they fight.

column2: Route 9, Courageous Cavern, Loop Lagoon, Frigid Sea
column3: Sword: It feeds on seaweed, using its teeth to scrape it off rocks. Electric current flows from the tips of its spines.\n\nShield: It stores electricity in each spine. Even if one gets broken off, it still continues to emit electricity for at least three hours.

column2: Route 8, 10, Lake of Outrage, Slippery Slope, Snowslide Slope, Path to the Peak
column3: Sword: It spits out thread imbued with a frigid sort of energy and uses it to tie its body to branches, disguising itself as an icicle while it sleeps.\n\nShield: It eats snow that piles up on the ground. The more snow it eats, the bigger and more impressive the spikes on its back grow.

Sword: Icy scales fall from its wings like snow as it flies over fields and mountains. The temperature of its wings is less than −290 degrees Fahrenheit.\n\nShield: It shows no mercy to any who desecrate fields and mountains. It will fly around on its icy wings, causing a blizzard to chase offenders away.

column2: Route 10, Lake of Outrage, Giant's Bed, Giant's Foot
column3: Sword: It stands in grasslands, watching the sun’s descent from zenith to horizon. This Pokémon has a talent for delivering dynamic kicks.\n\nShield: Once a year, on a specific date and at a specific time, they gather out of nowhere and form up in a circle.

Sword: It drifted in on the flow of ocean waters from a frigid place. It keeps its head iced constantly to make sure it stays nice and cold.\n\nShield: This Pokémon keeps its heat-sensitive head cool with ice. It fishes for its food, dangling its single hair into the sea to lure in prey.

column2: Glimwood Tangle, Lake of Outrage, Ballimere Lake
column3: Sword: It uses the horns on its head to sense the emotions of others. Males will act as valets for those they serve, looking after their every need.\n\nShield: Through its horns, it can pick up on the emotions of creatures around it. Positive emotions are the source of its strength.

column2: Route 7, 9, Lake of Outrage, Challenge Beach, Ballimere Lake
column3: Sword: As it eats the seeds stored up in its pocket-like pouches, this Pokémon is not just satisfying its constant hunger. It’s also generating electricity.\n\nShield: It carries electrically roasted seeds with it as if they’re precious treasures. No matter how much it eats, it always gets hungry again in short order.

Sword: It digs up the ground with its trunk. It’s also very strong, being able to carry loads of over five tons without any problem at all.\n\nShield: If a job requires serious strength, this Pokémon will excel at it. Its copper body tarnishes in the rain, turning a vibrant green color.

Sword: They came over from another region long ago and worked together with humans. Their green skin is resistant to water.\n\nShield: These Pokémon live in herds. Their trunks have incredible grip strength, strong enough to crush giant rocks into powder.

Sword: In ancient times, it was unbeatable thanks to its powerful lower body, but it went extinct anyway after it depleted all its plant-based food sources.\n\nShield: The powerful muscles in its tail generate its electricity. Compared to its lower body, its upper half is entirely too small.

Sword: The shaking of its freezing upper half is what generates its electricity. It has a hard time walking around.\n\nShield: This Pokémon lived on prehistoric seashores and was able to preserve food with the ice on its body. It went extinct because it moved so slowly.

Sword: Powerful legs and jaws made it the apex predator of its time. Its own overhunting of its prey was what drove it to extinction.\n\nShield: Its mighty legs are capable of running at speeds exceeding 40 mph, but this Pokémon can’t breathe unless it’s underwater.

Sword: Though it’s able to capture prey by freezing its surroundings, it has trouble eating the prey afterward because its mouth is on top of its head.\n\nShield: The skin on its face is impervious to attack, but breathing difficulties made this Pokémon go extinct anyway.

Sword: Its body resembles polished metal, and it’s both lightweight and strong. The only drawback is that it rusts easily.\n\nShield: The special metal that composes its body is very light, so this Pokémon has considerable agility. It lives in caves because it dislikes the rain.

Sword: After being reborn as a ghost Pokémon, Dreepy wanders the areas it used to inhabit back when it was alive in prehistoric seas.\n\nShield: If this weak Pokémon is by itself, a mere child could defeat it. But if Dreepy has friends to help it train, it can evolve and become much stronger.

Sword: It’s capable of flying faster than 120 mph. It battles alongside Dreepy and dotes on them until they successfully evolve.\n\nShield: Without a Dreepy to place on its head and care for, it gets so uneasy it’ll try to substitute any Pokémon it finds for the missing Dreepy.

Sword: When it isn’t battling, it keeps Dreepy in the holes on its horns. Once a fight starts, it launches the Dreepy like supersonic missiles.\n\nShield: Apparently the Dreepy inside Dragapult’s horns eagerly look forward to being launched out at Mach speeds.

Sword: Known as a legendary hero, this Pokémon absorbs metal particles, transforming them into a weapon it uses to battle.\n\nShield: This Pokémon has slumbered for many years. Some say it’s Zamazenta’s elder sister—others say the two Pokémon are rivals.

Sword: In times past, it worked together with a king of the people to save the Galar region. It absorbs metal that it then uses in battle.\n\nShield: This Pokémon slept for aeons while in the form of a statue. It was asleep for so long, people forgot that it ever existed.

Sword: The core on its chest absorbs energy emanating from the lands of the Galar region. This energy is what allows Eternatus to stay active.\n\nShield: It was inside a meteorite that fell 20,000 years ago. There seems to be a connection between this Pokémon and the Dynamax phenomenon.

Sword: Kubfu trains hard to perfect its moves. The moves it masters will determine which form it takes when it evolves.\n\nShield: If Kubfu pulls the long white hair on its head, its fighting spirit heightens and power wells up from the depths of its belly.

Sword: People call it the embodiment of rage. It’s said that this Pokémon’s terrifying expression and shout will rid the world of malevolence.\n\nShield: The energy released by this Pokémon’s fists forms shock waves that can blow away Dynamax Pokémon in just one hit.

Sword: Within dense forests, this Pokémon lives in a pack with others of its kind. It’s incredibly aggressive, and the other Pokémon of the forest fear it.\n\nShield: Once the vines on Zarude’s body tear off, they become nutrients in the soil. This helps the plants of the forest grow.

Sword: This Pokémon is a cluster of electrical energy. It’s said that removing the rings on Regieleki’s body will unleash the Pokémon’s latent power.\n\nShield: Its entire body is made up of a single organ that generates electrical energy. Regieleki is capable of creating all Galar’s electricity.

Sword: An academic theory proposes that Regidrago’s arms were once the head of an ancient dragon Pokémon. The theory remains unproven.\n\nShield: Its body is composed of crystallized dragon energy. Regidrago is said to have the powers of every dragon Pokémon.

Sword: Glastrier emits intense cold from its hooves. It’s also a belligerent Pokémon—anything it wants, it takes by force.\n\nShield: Glastrier has tremendous physical strength, and the mask of ice covering its face is 100 times harder than diamond.

Sword: It probes its surroundings with all its senses save one—it doesn’t use its sense of sight. Spectrier’s kicks are said to separate soul from body.\n\nShield: As it dashes through the night, Spectrier absorbs the life-force of sleeping creatures. It craves silence and solitude.

Sword: Calyrex is a merciful Pokémon, capable of providing healing and blessings. It reigned over the Galar region in times of yore.\n\nShield: Calyrex is known in legend as a king that ruled over Galar in ancient times. It has the power to cause hearts to mend and plants to spring forth.
